91.q: Eleven packs of Arham rice, each marked 5 kg, actually contain these weights (in kg): 4.97, 5.05, 5.08, 5.03, 5.00, 5.06, 4.98, 5.08, 5.04, 5.07, 5.00. What is the probability that a randomly chosen pack contains more than 5 kg of rice?

54.explanation: 0.757575… repeats the block 75, so it equals 75/99 = 25/33 (option A).

67.explanation: Together they complete 5(1/25 + 1/20) = 45/100 of the work. The remainder is 55/100 = 11/20 (option D).

71.explanation: The numerators are consecutive squares 1², 2², 3², 4²; the next is 5² = 25. The denominators rise from 22 to 25, so the next is 26: 25/26 (option C).

91.explanation: Six of the eleven listed pack weights exceed 5 kg, so the probability is 6/11 (option B).

60.q: A coin and a die are thrown at random. What is the probability that a composite number appears on the die and a tail appears on the coin?

60.explanation: The composite outcomes on a standard die are 4 and 6, so the probability is 2/6 = 1/3. A tail has probability 1/2. The independent events occur together with probability 1/3 × 1/2 = 1/6 (option A).
